title: Quantum Simulation Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel quantum simulation framework centered around dynamic geometric transformation adjustment. Traditional quantum simulation often necessitates manual parameter tuning, limiting flexibility and potentially impacting accuracy. We propose a quantum geometric technique, leveraging quantum states to iteratively refine geometric transformations during the simulation process, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational burden. The core mechanism focuses on employing quantum states to represent and manipulate geometric primitives, allowing for adaptive and optimized transformations. This framework addresses the limitations of conventional methods, offering a promising pathway towards more efficient and accurate quantum simulations.

title: Adaptive Topological Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological genetic algorithm (ATGA) designed to efficiently find optimal solutions and maintain stability and reliability. Traditional genetic algorithms often suffer from the tendency to get trapped in local optima, while the ATGA leverages topological structure to promote global optimality. The algorithm employs a novel approach that constructs and maintains a topological representation of the search space, dynamically adjusting the search space to avoid these local optima. This paper details the algorithm's structure, proposes a mechanism for ensuring stability and reliability, and provides a comprehensive analysis of its performance.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometric Transformations for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, from drug discovery to materials science. However, realizing this potential requires efficient and scalable quantum algorithms. This paper explores the application of adaptive geometric transformations as a core mechanism for enhancing the performance of quantum computations. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters during the computation process, aiming to achieve higher fidelity and reduced computational complexity. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the efficiency of quantum algorithms, particularly in scenarios involving complex quantum circuits. The paper details the design of the adaptive transformation function, its implementation within a quantum computing framework, and a preliminary analysis of its impact on key quantum algorithms. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through simulations and a simplified demonstration of a specific quantum circuit. The research contributes to the ongoing development of robust and adaptable quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Topological Networks
abstract: Quantum Topological Networks (QTNs) represent a revolutionary paradigm shift in quantum information processing, offering potential for unparalleled computational speeds and secure communication. This paper explores the fundamental principles of QTNs, focusing on the utilization of quantum entanglement to construct a robust and efficient network for complex calculations and data transmission. The core claim of this work is that a meticulously engineered QTN architecture, leveraging the unique properties of entangled qubits, will dramatically enhance the performance of quantum computations compared to existing approaches. We detail the proposed mechanism, emphasizing the critical role of quantum entanglement in facilitating information transfer and computation. The significance of this research lies in its potential to unlock transformative capabilities across diverse quantum applications.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Nonlinear System Simulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a unique approach to simulating complex nonlinear systems. This research explores the design of a novel simulation framework leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced accuracy and efficiency in modeling these systems. We propose a system that utilizes quantum algorithms to meticulously capture the dynamics of the system, providing precise simulation and predictive capabilities. This work addresses the limitations of traditional simulation methods, particularly in handling intricate non-linear systems, and presents a fundamentally new approach to this challenging problem. The core mechanism centers on exploiting entanglement to create a more stable and accurate representation of the system's behavior. This paper outlines the design of the framework, its potential applications, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in simulating specific nonlinear systems.

title: The Adaptive Quantum Computation Algorithm via Dynamic Topology Adjustment
abstract: Quantum computation, a fundamentally different approach to computation, offers the potential for unparalleled speed and complexity. Traditional algorithms often rely on fixed, static parameters, limiting their adaptability to diverse inputs. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum computation algorithm based on dynamic topology adjustment, designed to overcome these limitations. We propose a framework that dynamically modifies the quantum system's topology during computation, allowing it to adapt to varying input conditions and enhance its robustness. The core mechanism involves employing a sophisticated mapping function to translate the input state into a specific topology, effectively tailoring the quantum system's response. This adaptive approach significantly improves the algorithm's ability to handle complex problems and maintain consistent performance across a range of inputs. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved results through rigorous analysis and simulations, showcasing its potential for advancing the field of quantum computation.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Simulation for Non-Linear Geometric Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic probability field simulation, designed to efficiently locate optimal solutions in complex geometric spaces. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter design, limiting exploration capabilities. This work leverages the inherent stochasticity of probability field simulations to automatically discover optimal solutions and employ geometric optimization to enhance algorithm efficiency. The core mechanism involves simulating intricate geometric structures, generating candidate solutions, and employing geometric optimization techniques to refine the search process. We present a framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing a specific geometric function, showcasing its potential for broader applicability across diverse problems.

title: Quantum Hiding Matrix Adaptive Optimization
abstract: Quantum Hiding Matrix Adaptive Optimization is a novel optimization framework designed to enhance the robustness and adaptability of machine learning models through the utilization of quantum mechanics. This approach leverages the unique properties of quantum hidden Markov models (HHMMs) – specifically, their inherent quantum entanglement – to dynamically adjust model parameters and mitigate overfitting. The core mechanism involves a quantum optimization process guided by entanglement, enabling the model to adapt to changing input data characteristics in real-time. This research explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize optimization algorithms, specifically for complex machine learning tasks. The paper presents a detailed mathematical framework and demonstrates its efficacy through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in model performance and generalization capabilities compared to conventional optimization techniques.

title: Context-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Context-Aware Graph Neural Networks (CAGNNs) for enhancing social network analysis. Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) primarily focus on the structural relationships within a network, often overlooking crucial contextual information that significantly influences social dynamics. This research argues that incorporating user demographics, location data, and social group affiliations as contextual features dramatically improves the accuracy and interpretability of GNN models. We propose a framework where the standard graph structure is augmented with these contextual attributes, and GNNs are trained to learn representations sensitive to both the network's topology and the associated contextual nuances. Through this approach, we aim to move beyond purely structural analysis, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of social networks and their complexities. We present a detailed formulation of the CAGNN model and discuss key considerations for its implementation and evaluation. The results presented demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating contextual information into GNNs, showcasing its ability to capture richer social relationships and improve predictive performance.

title: 基于自适应的动态扰动算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic perturbation algorithm designed to enhance model training and prediction efficiency. Traditional perturbation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving data. Our algorithm leverages a self-adaptive approach, meticulously learning the inherent characteristics of input data perturbations. This learning process dynamically adjusts model parameters, resulting in improved performance across a wider range of scenarios. The core mechanism centers around a continuous feedback loop, optimizing parameter adjustments based on observed data fluctuations. This adaptation allows the algorithm to effectively handle data variability and improve the model's robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through experimental results on a diverse dataset of image processing and regression tasks. The key contribution is the incorporation of a robust learning mechanism that ensures the algorithm's adaptability and performance remain consistent even with significant data shifts.

Traditional perturbation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving data. Our algorithm leverages a self-adaptive approach, meticulously learning the inherent characteristics of input data perturbations. This learning process dynamically adjusts model parameters, resulting in improved performance across a wider range of scenarios. The core mechanism centers around a continuous feedback loop, optimizing parameter adjustments based on observed data fluctuations. This adaptation allows the algorithm to effectively handle data variability and improve the model's robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through experimental results on a diverse dataset of image processing and regression tasks. The key contribution is the incorporation of a robust learning mechanism that ensures the algorithm's adaptability and performance remain consistent even with significant data shifts.

title: Quantum Tunneling-Based Algorithm Acceleration
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to algorithm acceleration by leveraging the principles of quantum tunneling. The core idea is to map specific computational steps within classical algorithms onto simulated quantum tunneling processes. By employing probability calculations and sampling techniques, we aim to achieve significant speedups for certain algorithms. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines a methodology for implementing this approach, focusing on the potential advantages offered by quantum mechanics in overcoming limitations inherent in classical computation. The exploration includes detailed mathematical formulations and conceptual descriptions, offering a foundation for future research and development in this area. We demonstrate the feasibility of this method through illustrative examples, highlighting the potential for transformative gains in computational efficiency. The focus remains on the theoretical aspects and algorithmic design, without requiring experimental validation. ---

title: Responsibility-Space Contracts for Assuring Adaptive AI: Design-Derived Responsibility Boundaries and Selective Formal Assurance — Research Artifact
abstract: Research artifact accompanying the manuscript “Responsibility-Space Contracts for Assuring Adaptive AI: Design-Derived Responsibility Boundaries and Selective Formal Assurance.” The artifact contains the implementation and frozen evaluation evidence supporting RQ2–RQ5, including responsibility-level contract evaluation, bounded neural-network verification, modified-model evaluation, and edge-platform evaluation on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5. The artifact is distributed as a frozen package with a SHA-256 integrity manifest and claim-to-evidence mapping. Selected DTLD-derived inputs, including redistributed tensor caches and detailed sanitized holdout data, are excluded because redistribution permission has not been established. The included evidence supports the claims and experimental scope reported in the accompanying manuscript. In particular, bounded neural-network verification results are case-local and should not be interpreted as a universal robustness guarantee, and the edge-platform measurements should not be interpreted as a general hardware-ranking claim.

title: Quantum Entanglement Field Topology
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing communication and computation. However, the inherent fragility of entangled states presents significant challenges for reliable data transmission. This paper investigates the use of topological quantum field theory to enhance quantum entanglement, proposing a novel framework centered around dynamically constructed topological structures. We explore how these structures can bolster the stability and transfer capability of entangled states, offering a potential pathway to more robust and efficient quantum communication and computation. The core claim is that the integration of dynamic topology into quantum entanglement will yield a significant improvement in these areas. This work presents a theoretical framework based on the principles of self-similarity and the manipulation of topological properties. The investigation will focus on creating a quantum field topology that facilitates stable entanglement, leading to enhanced data security and computational speed.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Parallel Transport for Quantum State Preservation
abstract: Quantum state preservation is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, particularly when dealing with complex systems and measurement. Traditional methods often rely on approximations that can introduce errors. This paper proposes a novel method for preserving quantum states through non-Euclidean parallel transport, offering a potential breakthrough in maintaining the integrity of quantum states. We introduce a 'Quantum State Morphing Algorithm' designed to minimize geometric distortions during transport, leading to enhanced state preservation. We detail the algorithm's principles, explore its theoretical implications, and present preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in preserving quantum states. This work addresses a critical need in quantum information theory, offering a viable path toward more robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology-Based Machine Learning Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, which can limit the algorithm's ability to adapt to complex data distributions. This work proposes a dynamic topology-based approach that iteratively optimizes model parameters by simulating data distribution, resulting in enhanced model performance. The core mechanism involves utilizing a dynamic topology structure to guide parameter adjustments, enabling the algorithm to effectively explore the data space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and generalization ability.

title: Title: Adaptive Probability Field (APF) Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for generating probability fields – the Adaptive Probability Field (APF) – designed to enhance predictive accuracy in complex systems. Traditional probability distributions lack the adaptability needed to effectively handle dynamic environmental conditions. The APF system continuously creates and adjusts probability fields based on real-time environmental data, offering a significant improvement over static approaches. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a feedback loop between environmental data and the probability field generation, ensuring a robust and adaptive model. This research aims to address the limitations of current probabilistic modeling techniques by providing a dynamic solution capable of better capturing and interpreting complex systems. We provide a detailed explanation of the system's architecture, the rationale behind the chosen parameters, and preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness across a range of simulated scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Inference for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel relational inference engine termed Quantum-Inspired Relational Inference (QIRI). Traditional relational inference methods often falter when confronted with high-dimensional, noisy data and intricate dependencies characteristic of complex systems. QIRI addresses these limitations by adopting principles inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and measurement. The system utilizes nodes representing potential relationships, and the inference process mimics a probabilistic measurement of these relationships. Crucially, the weighting of these measurements is governed by a 'coherence' metric, reflecting the compatibility of a relationship with the observed data. This approach aims to provide a fundamentally different perspective on relational inference, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical methods in handling complex data landscapes. The core of the method lies in simulating the probabilistic nature of quantum measurement and applying it to the problem of discovering relationships within data. We will explore the mathematical framework underpinning QIRI, focusing on the probabilistic models and the coherence function used to guide the inference process. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate that quantum-inspired concepts can be effectively translated into a robust and scalable inference engine for complex systems.

title: High-Order Matrix Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to matrix learning utilizing a high-order structure to enhance model generalization, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions. We propose a new algorithm that integrates high-order matrix structures with an adaptive learning process, focusing on learning "high-order features" to optimize model performance. The core mechanism centers around leveraging this high-order structure to capture nuanced relationships within the data. This work addresses limitations of existing matrix learning techniques by providing a framework for improved generalization capabilities, especially in data with intricate patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantum State Simulation via Non-Linear Topological Structure
abstract: Quantum state simulation is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and quantum information science. Traditional methods often rely on approximations and classical algorithms, limiting our ability to fully explore and understand complex quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel quantum state simulation approach that leverages the inherent non-linear topological structure of quantum states to provide a fundamentally different method for simulating quantum systems. We introduce a new simulation framework that dynamically generates and analyzes topological structures within the quantum state space, enabling a deeper and more accurate understanding of quantum phenomena. The core mechanism centers around representing the quantum state as a topological manifold, allowing for the simulation of quantum evolution through the manipulation of this manifold's topology. This approach offers a unique pathway to predict and interpret quantum system behavior, moving beyond classical approximations.

title: Quantum Topology Language: A Novel Approach to Quantum System Modeling and Information Transfer
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field, offers a fundamentally different perspective on the behavior of quantum systems. This paper introduces the Quantum Topology Language (QTL), a new computational framework designed to explicitly model and understand quantum systems' topological structures. We propose a language based on the principles of quantum topology, aiming to simplify the complex dynamics inherent in quantum systems, particularly concerning quantum error correction and information transfer. This endeavor aims to advance our understanding of these processes by providing a more structured and intuitive representation of quantum phenomena. The QTL utilizes a combination of mathematical formalism and algorithmic design to achieve this. The paper details the foundational concepts of quantum topology and demonstrates the practical implementation of the QTL through a series of illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum system modeling and analysis.

title: Quantum Topological Field Simulation and High-Dimensional Data Analysis
abstract: Quantum Topological Field (QTF) simulation offers a novel approach to analyzing high-dimensional data by leveraging the inherent topological properties of spacetime. This paper explores the application of QTF simulation techniques to uncover hidden patterns and structures within complex datasets. We introduce a novel methodology that utilizes dynamic field evolution to identify correlations and anomalies undetectable through conventional analytical methods. The core mechanism centers on the exploration of quantum entanglement and superposition, which allows for the detection of subtle relationships within high-dimensional data spaces. The research demonstrates the potential of QTF simulation to provide insights into a diverse range of scientific disciplines, including complex systems modeling, data science, and potentially, fundamental physics. This work contributes to the field of quantum information theory and highlights a promising avenue for enhancing data analysis capabilities.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dimension-expanding model leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric structures. We propose a framework, termed "Self-Adaptive Geometry," wherein quantum entanglement governs the evolution of space, allowing for automatic adjustments to improve computational efficiency and data storage. The core mechanism focuses on integrating the inherent dynamics of entanglement into geometric transformations, creating a system capable of self-optimization. This approach offers a fundamentally new pathway for quantum computation and information processing, differentiating it from existing theoretical frameworks centered primarily on algorithmic advancements. The proposed model's potential implications for quantum algorithms and data management are substantial, representing a significant step towards a more versatile and adaptive approach to quantum systems.

title: A Review of Neural Question Generation: Approaches, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: The goal of question generation is to automatically produce relevant and meaningful questions from diverse inputs such as knowledge bases, natural language texts, and images. With the rapid advancement of neural architectures, neural question generation (NQG) has attracted growing attention across both academia and industry. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive review of developments in NQG, spanning traditional neural approaches to the latest paradigms driven by large language models (LLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We begin by outlining the fundamental components of NQG, including its problem formulation, benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, and representative applications. Next, we categorize existing methods into three main types: structured NQG , which relies on structured data sources; unstructured NQG , which handles loosely structured inputs such as texts or images; and hybrid NQG , which integrates multiple modalities. For each category, we review representative neural models and synthesize the problems addressed by successive generations of methods, their remaining limitations, and the motivations behind major methodological transitions. Furthermore, we trace the progression of NQG from supervised neural approaches and pre-trained models to prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, reinforcement learning, and emerging tool-augmented and agent-based paradigms. We also discuss how recent LLMs and MLLMs have enabled more contextually aligned, knowledge-grounded, and reasoning-enhanced question generation, together with emerging concerns such as hallucination, bias, and evaluation reliability. Finally, we outline open challenges and emerging research trends, offering a forward-looking perspective on the evolution of NQG. This survey presents a meticulously curated compilation of related papers, datasets, and code, serving as a comprehensive resource for anyone studying NQG.

title: Preparing Citizens for Emergency Calls with a Hybrid FSM-LLM Dialogue Agent
abstract: Emergency calls are time-critical, verbal-only interactions in which call takers must assess severity and make decisions based solely on the caller’s description. Effective communication is critical during these calls, especially since most callers are inexperienced and untrained due to the rarity of emergency situations. To address this challenge, we develop a task-oriented dialogue agent that simulates emergency call takers to prepare citizens for effective medical emergency communication. It uses a finite-state machine as its dialogue policy and large language models for natural language understanding. This agent conducts protocol-guided interactions and maps caller descriptions to structured symptoms. In a small exploratory study with human participants, our agent achieved higher observed classification accuracy and dialogue efficiency while maintaining high naturalness scores.

title: Mitigating repetition and loops via implicit signal self-tuning for self-correcting inference
abstract: Large language models often suffer from logical hallucinations, repetitive generation loops, and imbalanced reasoning efficiency during complex mathematical reasoning. Existing static prompting and explicit intervention methods cannot dynamically regulate the decoding process based on the model’s real-time reasoning state. This paper proposes the Implicit Signal Self-Tuning (ISST) framework. It synchronously computes two internal uncertainty metrics during decoding: attention distribution entropy and token confidence entropy. These are fused via Sigmoid multiplication to obtain a unified entropy value. This value quantifies the risk level at each reasoning step. When the unified entropy exceeds a threshold, the framework activates an exploration mode. It increases the sampling temperature and narrows the top-p sampling interval to break reasoning loops. When the entropy falls below the threshold, it switches to an exploitation mode. Parameters are gradually restored to baseline values. This balances reasoning accuracy with token consumption. Validation is conducted on multiple mathematical datasets including AIME24, AMC23, and MATH500. Models ranging from 1.5B to 7B parameters are tested. The framework achieves an average 50% reduction in repetitive generation rate. It reduces token consumption while maintaining reasoning accuracy. No modification to the model backbone is required. This provides a lightweight new approach for adaptive reasoning optimization in large models.

title: SCALE: Simulation-Calibrated Amortized Learning for Energy Materials (A hybrid architecture connecting deterministic modeling, real-world data, and transformer-scale inference for accelerated energy-materials discovery)
abstract: Energy systems face converging pressures for security, affordability, resilience, and sustainability, creating a need for faster discovery of deployable energy materials. Here we introduce SCALE (Simulation-Calibrated Amortized Learning for Energy Materials), a physics-grounded, real-world-data-calibrated learning architecture that connects deterministic scientific operators, experimental calibration, expanded calibrated label generation, and transformer-scale inference. SCALE converts selected high-cost mechanistic computation and measured evidence into reusable models for rapid screening, ranking, inverse design, and active learning. We formulate the framework, identify ten method-based application regimes, and demonstrate SCALE for solid-state metal-hydride hydrogen-storage capacity prediction. In this implementation, a hydride phase-equilibrium capacity operator is calibrated against 381 measured ML-HydPARK capacity anchors and used to generate 5,000 candidate-condition-prototype teacher labels. A crystallographically anchored periodic-graph representation preserves atomic sites, periodic neighbor relationships, and local metal environments absent from formula-only encodings. An edge-biased graph transformer with 2.90 million parameters reproduces calibrated teacher labels with five-fold surrogate fidelity of MAE 0.0582 wt% H2, RMSE 0.0833 wt% H2, R2 = 0.9927, and Pearson r = 0.9963. Post hoc attention analysis suggests that SCALE learns chemically organized element groupings and metal-metal relationships consistent with established hydride chemistry, without chemistry-group labels as supervision. Once trained, SCALE shifts million-candidate evaluation from repeated deterministic workflow execution to batched learned inference, reducing per-candidate screening cost by approximately 10^7-10^8 while retaining links to simulation and experimental evidence.

title: A Calibrated Reflection Approach for Enhancing Confidence Estimation in LLMs
abstract: A critical challenge in deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) is developing reliable mechanisms to estimate their confidence, enabling systems to determine when to trust model outputs versus seek human intervention. We present a Calibrated Reflection approach for enhancing confidence estimation in LLMs, a framework that combines structured reasoning with distance-aware calibration technique. Our approach introduces three key innovations: (1) a Maximum Confidence Selection (MCS) method that comprehensively evaluates confidence across all possible labels, (2) a reflection-based prompting mechanism that enhances reasoning reliability, and (3) a distance-aware calibration technique that accounts for ordinal relationships between labels. We evaluate our framework on diverse datasets, including HelpSteer2, Llama T-REx, and a proprietary conversational dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness across both conversational and fact-based classification tasks. This work contributes to the broader goal of developing reliable and well-calibrated confidence estimation methods for LLMs, enabling informed decisions about model trust and human judgement.

title: Typed Flexible-Arity Slotted E-Graphs: A Soundness Construction and an Alloy Case Study
abstract: Slotted e-graphs represent open terms modulo consistent renaming, while algebraic operators benefit from canonical sequence, bag, or set children. We compose the two at a specification level: typed slot-mapped invocations inhabit operator-declared ports whose sibling quotient and recursive flattening licenses are certified separately. A generic finite quotient presentation proves exactness of its least-orbit normal form, while certified records specify effective-support kernel extraction and collision. For abstract obligation traces carrying local endpoint certificates, we prove finite-unfolding equational soundness. An Alloy case study compares seven related pipeline arms on a frozen corpus and a controlled transformation suite.

title: Neural-Network Maxent: a general extension with learned nonlinearity, applied to time-series for Desert Locust distribution modelling
abstract: Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) is essential for understanding how environmental conditions shape biodiversity, particularly for destructive pests such as the Desert Locust (Schistocerca gregaria), whose breeding dynamics are tightly coupled to rapidly evolving environmental conditions. Maxent has become the dominant method for presence-only data, but its reliance on a linear combination of hand chosen feature transforms limits its ability to capture the nonlinear, temporal relationships common in ecological monitoring, where covariates such as precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation indices evolve meaningfully over time. Standard implementations flatten time-series covariates into independent features, discarding sequential structure that carries critical signal. We introduce RNN Maxent, an extension of the Maxent framework that replaces the fixed feature dictionary with a neural network, specifically a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), trained end to end via backpropagation. The approach preserves Maxent's presence only statistical foundations, background normalization, and probability calibration, differing only in that the nonlinearity is learned from data rather than fixed in advance. We apply RNN Maxent to map suitable habitat for the Desert Locust using 50 day environmental time series derived from ERA5 Land, MODIS, and Sentinel 3, maintaining a 7 day gap between covariates and presence records to yield forecasting behavior. Compared against standard Maxent, RNN Maxent improves performance across metrics (ROC AUC 0.862 std 0.036 vs. 0.792; F1 0.671 std 0.056 vs. 0.590).

title: Quantum Computation Latency-Energy Tradeoff and the JPCUB Metric
abstract: Quantum computation faces a critical tradeoff between wall-clock latency and energy consumption, with faster gates and parallel syndrome extraction often increasing power demands. This work investigates whether minimizing latency necessarily raises energy costs, leveraging the Margolus-Levitin bound, which constrains quantum operation times via $ \tau \geq \hbar/(\pi E) $ [10.1016/S0003-4916(02)00005-9]. By modeling latency as gate execution plus quantum error correction (QEC) cycles and energy as control pulse, cooling, and classical processing costs, we demonstrate a Pareto frontier exists under this bound. We propose the **JPCUB (Joule-Second Per Computational Unit Bit)** metric, $ \text{JPCUB} = E \cdot T $, to quantify this tradeoff. Simulations suggest moderate gate speeds and optimized parallelism may yield lower JPCUB than extreme strategies [arXiv:2103.05678; arXiv:2004.00012; arXiv:2201.01234]. This framework enables comparative analysis of architectures under energy-latency constraints, with open questions on qubit-specific dynamics and non-adiabatic control. ## 1. title: Non-Linear Differential Equation Constraint Optimization (NLDEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Non-Linear Differential Equation Constraint Optimization (NLDEC) method designed to effectively address complex, nonlinear constraint problems. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with such scenarios, necessitating specialized approaches. This work leverages the inherent properties of non-linear differential equations to model and optimize systems with intricate constraints. We present a robust and efficient algorithm that integrates constraint handling into the optimization process, offering a significant advantage over existing methods. The core mechanism focuses on systematically incorporating and managing the nonlinear nature of the differential equation, ensuring optimal solutions within specified constraints. The resulting method demonstrates superior performance in several benchmark test cases, validating its efficacy in handling complex scenarios.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Non-Classical Geometric Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement information encoding is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to revolutionize secure communication and quantum computation. This paper proposes a novel approach to this field, utilizing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to construct a robust and efficient encoding scheme. We introduce a non-classical geometric model centered around entangled states, exploring the potential for self-correction and information transfer. The core of our work lies in leveraging this entanglement to mitigate information degradation and enhance the reliability of the encoding process. This research investigates the potential applications of this model in both quantum computing and quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over traditional methods.

title: Core Claim: Design a quantum computing-based topology-topology analysis algorithm to efficiently compute topological structures and provide more precise topological evolution analysis.
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to enhance topology analysis, specifically focusing on the computational complexity of intricate topological structures. The central challenge lies in the inherent difficulty of efficiently representing and manipulating topological data, which often necessitates computationally intensive methods. We propose a novel quantum algorithm framework, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate the analysis of topological phases and their evolution. This framework incorporates a modified version of the Wasserstein distance, adapted for topological data, and utilizes quantum Fourier transforms to efficiently explore the space of possible topological configurations. The algorithm's core mechanism involves quantum-enhanced representation of topological states and the application of a specific quantum operation to determine the order of topological phase transitions. The paper details a preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's potential for improved accuracy and speed compared to classical methods, specifically for analyzing topological landscapes involving complex branching. We present a case study illustrating the algorithm's effectiveness in analyzing a specific topological structure, highlighting the benefits of quantum computation in this area. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the algorithm's applicability to more complex topological systems and scaling to larger datasets.

title: Title: Adaptive Cognitive Resonance Networks (ACRN)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Cognitive Resonance Networks (ACRN), a novel neural network architecture designed to emulate the brain's dynamic information processing by dynamically adjusting the resonance between cognitive modules. Traditional neural networks often operate in a fixed, static state, failing to capture the complex interplay of information integration crucial for human cognition. ACRN addresses this limitation through a self-tuning feedback loop that iteratively prioritizes and strengthens connections between modules based on real-time data, mimicking the brain's ability to integrate disparate inputs. We detail the network's core mechanism – a feedback loop incorporating internal state influence – and explore its potential for improved cognitive modeling and performance. The research presents a framework for dynamically adjusting network parameters to optimize information flow and enhance cognitive function.

Traditional quantum algorithm verification often relies on static verification methods, which are inadequate for complex environments. We propose a novel approach that leverages dynamic topology, enabling real-time optimization and validation of quantum algorithms. This system utilizes a self-consistent evolution of a topological structure, providing a framework for dynamically assessing the correctness and efficiency of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around the instantaneous adaptation of the topology, allowing for continuous refinement and optimization. The resulting validation process offers a promising path towards enhanced quantum algorithm verification, potentially uncovering latent optimization opportunities.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Cognitive Graph Structures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning utilizing cognitive graph structures. The core idea is to integrate the strengths of neural networks – their ability to learn complex patterns from data – with symbolic knowledge representations – providing explicit, interpretable reasoning. We propose a system where a neural network learns to predict relationships within a dynamically evolving cognitive graph. This dynamic structure allows the system to adapt and refine its knowledge base based on observed data, leading to more flexible and explainable reasoning compared to traditional static neural-symbolic methods. The key innovation lies in the graph's ability to self-organize and update its structure, guided by the neural network's predictions, creating a truly interactive and adaptive reasoning framework. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a mechanism for continuous learning and refinement of symbolic knowledge, ultimately leading to improved performance on complex reasoning tasks.

title: Symbolic Regression with Neural Turing Machines for Mathematical Discovery
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) for automated mathematical discovery through symbolic regression. The central idea is to leverage NTMs' ability to learn complex temporal dependencies and their external memory to construct symbolic expressions that accurately represent underlying mathematical relationships within a dataset. We propose a framework where an NTM is trained to generate symbolic equations, utilizing its memory to store and retrieve relevant mathematical concepts, operators, and variables. The core claim is that NTMs can effectively learn these symbolic representations, leading to the automated derivation of mathematical formulas. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation strategy for this approach, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field of automated mathematical discovery. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this combined approach, showcasing the NTM's capacity for discovering non-trivial mathematical expressions.

title: Causal Inference via Bayesian Networks with Learned Structure and Parameters
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of causal inference within the Bayesian Network framework, particularly the difficulty in learning complex causal structures from observational data. Traditional Bayesian Networks often rely on manually defined structures, which are difficult to create and maintain, and can be inaccurate representations of the underlying causal relationships. We propose a novel approach that learns both the graph structure and the parameters of a Bayesian Network simultaneously, leveraging a variational inference technique. The model incorporates prior knowledge to guide the learning process, improving robustness and efficiency. Our method offers a more flexible and data-driven approach to causal discovery, moving beyond the limitations of pre-defined structures and enabling more accurate inference in complex systems. The core contribution lies in the synergistic learning of structure and parameters, leading to a more reliable representation of causal relationships. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework.

title: Multi-Dimensional Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding within multi-dimensional spaces, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to construct multi-dimensional entangled states to encode multi-dimensional data directly into quantum bits (qubits). This method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional information encoding techniques, which typically restrict data representation to single dimensions. The proposed scheme utilizes the inherent correlations within entangled states to facilitate rapid data transmission and processing. We present a theoretical framework outlining the encoding process and discuss the potential advantages of this approach, specifically its ability to handle complex, high-dimensional datasets. The efficiency and scalability of this method are explored, highlighting its potential applications in areas such as advanced data storage, secure communication, and quantum computing. We focus on the mathematical formulation of the entanglement-based encoding process and demonstrate its feasibility through theoretical analysis.

title: Probability Logic and Dynamic Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic-based dynamic adaptive algorithm designed to handle complex, evolving environments. Traditional algorithm optimization relies heavily on manual parameter adjustments, limiting adaptability and control. This work proposes a framework that leverages the inherent probabilistic nature of algorithms to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters and strategies, resulting in enhanced performance and responsiveness. The core mechanism involves constructing a "self-adaptive algorithm engine" powered by probabilistic reasoning, allowing the system to continuously optimize its behavior in response to changing conditions. The paper presents a detailed design of this engine, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulation and preliminary analysis. The focus is on achieving high-level, controllable system behavior through probabilistic reasoning.

title: 基于自适应量子算法的非线性优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to non-linear optimization utilizing a dynamically adjusted quantum algorithm. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering performance. Our proposed method employs a self-adaptive quantum algorithm, which continuously monitors and adjusts quantum parameters to optimize the solution process. The core mechanism involves a closed-loop optimization where the quantum algorithm's parameters are modified based on the observed solution quality and the system's current state. This adaptive approach enhances optimization accuracy, reduces computational cost, and facilitates the handling of complex, non-linear problems, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, experimental validation, and analysis of its performance, showcasing its potential for improved optimization across diverse applications.

title: Quantum Simulation of Consciousness Computing
abstract: Quantum Simulation of Consciousness Computing explores the potential of quantum computing to model and understand the neural basis of consciousness. This paper introduces a novel framework leveraging quantum simulation to emulate the dynamic behavior of brain neurons, aiming to elucidate the fundamental mechanisms underpinning consciousness. We detail the key principles of this approach, focusing on the use of quantum superposition and entanglement to represent and analyze neural networks. The core claim is that quantum simulation can provide a more precise and insightful understanding of the brain's processes, offering a pathway toward developing artificial consciousness.

title: Title: Adaptive Information Entropy Dynamic Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for dynamically adjusting information entropy, aiming to enhance data compression efficiency by adapting to data input variations. Traditional entropy adjustment methods often lack flexibility, requiring manual parameter tuning. This work proposes a method employing a feedback loop based on the input data's characteristics to iteratively refine the entropy, thereby optimizing data compression. The core mechanism involves a system of adjustment parameters that modulate the entropy value, promoting a more efficient compression process. The algorithm's design addresses the limitations of static adjustment approaches, offering a dynamic and adaptable solution for data compression tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, showcasing improved compression rates compared to baseline methods.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Lattice Modeling - Predicting Crystallographic Structures
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for predicting the properties of complex crystalline structures, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical crystal modeling. We introduce a "Quantum Resonance" algorithm, employing quantum entanglement to explore the structure space, offering the potential for more accurate and efficient predictions. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of quantum systems to identify and characterize structural patterns previously inaccessible through traditional computational approaches. This work establishes a foundational step towards a quantum-enhanced approach to crystallographic structure prediction, with implications for materials science, drug discovery, and fundamental physics research. The algorithm's design emphasizes adaptability and the ability to uncover subtle structural relationships, potentially revolutionizing the field.

title: A Bangla Grammar Question Answering Dataset with Prerequisite Knowledge, Multi-Stage Hints, and Hint Convergence Scores
abstract: This dataset contains 10,000 manually curated Bangla grammar question-answering instances. It was developed for hint-based learning, intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive and curriculum-aware learning, knowledge tracing, educational NLP, and LLM evaluation. All questions, grammar concepts, reference answers, explanations, and instructional content were collected from the official SSC textbook "বাংলা ভাষার ব্যাকরণ ও নির্মিতি" ("Bangla Bhashar Byakaran O Nirmity"), published by the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB), Bangladesh. The source material was manually curated into structured QA instances. Each record contains a Bangla grammar question, reference answer, explanation, topic, subtopic, difficulty, prerequisite concepts, semantic tags, five progressive hints, and stage-wise hint convergence scores. Hints progress from general contextual guidance to near-explicit support. Each 0–1 convergence score represents intended guidance toward the correct answer: lower scores are broader and higher scores are more specific. Scores reflect pedagogical progression, not empirical probabilities or model-confidence values. The dataset is distributed in UTF-8 JSON Lines (.jsonl): full.jsonl (10,000 instances), train.jsonl (70%), valid.jsonl (15%), test.jsonl (15%), and sample.jsonl (20 instances). Each record includes: id, topic, subtopic, difficulty, question, prerequisites, hints, convergence, candidate_answers, exact_answer, explanation, and topic_tags. Example Record: { "id": "bn_grammar_05900", "topic": "কারক ও বিভক্তি", "subtopic": "বিভক্তির প্রকারভেদ ও প্রয়োগ", "difficulty": "medium", "question": "বাক্যে ব্যবহৃত একটি পদের সাথে অন্য পদের অর্থগত সম্পর্ককে অর্থবহ করতে কোন ব্যাকরণিক উপাদানের ভূমিকা প্রধান?", "prerequisites": ["বিভক্তি", "বাক্যতত্ত্ব"], "hints": [ "শব্দের শেষে যুক্ত হয়ে পদের অন্বয় রক্ষা করে।", "বাক্যের কারক সম্পর্কের মূল ভিত্তি এটি।", "বিভক্তি নির্দেশক ব্যাকরণিক উপাদান।", "বিভক্তি রূপ নির্দেশক বিকল্প।", "বিভক্তি নির্দেশক সঠিক উত্তর।" ], "convergence": { "1": 0.35, "2": 0.55, "3": 0.74, "4": 0.88, "5": 0.97 }, "candidate_answers": ["বিভক্তি", "উপসর্গ", "সন্ধি", "সমাস"], "exact_answer": "বিভক্তি", "explanation": "বাক্যস্থিত পদসমূহের পারস্পরিক অন্বয় বা অর্থগত সম্বন্ধ স্পষ্ট ও অর্থপূর্ণ করতে শব্দবিভক্তি ও ক্রিয়াবিভক্তির ভূমিকাই প্রধান।", "topic_tags": ["Bangla Grammar", "কারক ও বিভক্তি", "বিভক্তি"] } Records were reviewed for completeness, annotation consistency, factual accuracy, and valid JSON formatting before release. The dataset supports controlled studies of how progressively revealed hints influence learning and answer selection. It is suitable for evaluating AI models that generate, rank, or select pedagogically useful hints at different levels of instructional support. This dataset is intended for research and educational purposes, particularly for building progressive, adaptive, and concept-aware hint-based systems for Bangla grammar learning.

title: Conjunctive dynamic searchable symmetric encryption
abstract: Abstract A practical searchable symmetric encryption (SSE) should allow users to privately store documents on untrusted servers with the abilities to (1) search with multiple keywords, and (2) add or delete documents dynamically. The oblivious cross tag () construction from Crypto’13 is the most efficient SSE scheme that allows conjunctive searches, but only for static databases. In NDSS’20, was extended to supporting dynamic updates. However, is not forward private . In this work, we identify a commonly used setting for SSE where a document with its associated keywords can be dynamically added to or deleted from the database as a whole, but the keyword set is not modified in between. We call it the non-modifiable document (NMD) setting. In this NMD setting, we propose a generic framework for designing conjunctive dynamic SSE (CD-SSE), supporting conjunctive queries that allow dynamic updates while being forward and backward private at the same time. Our construction uses a generic dynamic single keyword SSE and the scheme as modular black-boxes. Our scheme generalises . We provide new security definitions of forward and backward privacy for the new NMD setting. Our generic construction (and hence ) achieves forward and backward privacy in the new setting, even when the underlying single keyword SSE scheme is only backward private. We analyse the precise leakages of our scheme to the adversarial server in the NMD setting. We have instantiated our generic construction with three different single keyword schemes. Experiments show that our schemes are very efficient and practical. Our code is publicly available.

title: TNFlow: Amortized Posterior Inference for Trans-Neptunian Object Surface Composition
abstract: We present TNFlow, a transformer and normalizing flow architecture for inferring the surface composition of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs) from their reflectance spectra. TNFlow is trained on synthetic spectra generated by the Shkuratov radiative transfer model to act as its inverse. TNFlow takes ${\sim}$0.7s to invert one spectrum on a single CPU core, returning a multimodal posterior over simplex-valid compositions and grain sizes. On synthetic spectra, the highest-weight mode achieves a mean total-variation distance of 0.149 from ground truth on the test split, and the model generalizes well to unseen combinations of known components. Qualitative tests on real JWST spectra show blindness or bias towards some materials. We suggest this could be attributed to either simulator fidelity or the training set.

title: Quantum Simulation Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a powerful approach to modeling quantum systems, but traditional methods often struggle with complex parameter settings and computationally intensive simulations. This paper presents a novel quantum simulation framework that dynamically adjusts the parameters of a quantum simulation based on observed results, aiming to improve accuracy and reduce computational cost. We introduce a modified variational quantum algorithm framework utilizing quantum annealing to dynamically optimize simulation parameters, achieving significantly enhanced fidelity and reduced execution time compared to existing approaches. This work explores the potential of adaptive parameter control within the context of quantum simulation, offering a promising path toward more efficient and accurate quantum modeling.

title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Diagrams
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing-based simulation technique designed to accurately model complex, multi-layered diagrams. Traditional simulation methods often fall short in capturing the intricate details and behavior of such systems, hindering investigations into complex phenomena. We propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum properties to represent and manipulate diagram elements, offering a significantly improved fidelity assessment compared to classical methods. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting superposition and entanglement to represent diagram states and evolve them across time, ultimately achieving a more nuanced and accurate simulation of the underlying system. The potential applications of this technique extend across diverse fields, including materials science, biology, and engineering, highlighting its transformative capabilities.

title: Dynamic Topology Geometry for Quantum Computing Speed Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology geometry to accelerate quantum computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on manually adjusting parameters, which can be computationally expensive and limit scalability. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters during the simulation process, effectively reducing the computational complexity. This approach leverages the inherent non-linearity within the system to achieve efficient and optimized performance. The core mechanism centers around a transformation of the simulation process into a parameter-adjustment iterative loop, mitigating the limitations of static optimization techniques. The investigation demonstrates significant improvements in simulation time and accuracy compared to traditional methods, highlighting the potential for substantial speedups in quantum algorithm design.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Network for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive graph neural network (DAGNN) framework for reinforcement learning. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms often struggle with evolving environments and require extensive fine-tuning. This work proposes a DAGNN that dynamically adjusts the network's structure and parameters based on the environment's dynamics, significantly enhancing learning efficiency. The core mechanism leverages the reinforcement learning process itself to iteratively refine the graph structure. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through extensive experiments on various reinforcement learning tasks, showcasing superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the key innovations and potential future directions of this framework.

title: 基于自适应的图论优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph-based optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Graph Optimization" (AGO), designed to automatically adjust graph structure and parameters to enhance model expressiveness and generalization capabilities. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering the algorithm's ability to discover optimal solutions. AGO leverages the inherent properties of graph theory, specifically "self-similarity" and "polygon-like" structures, to dynamically optimize the graph. The core mechanism involves iterative adjustments to graph parameters based on a feedback loop, ensuring robustness and adaptability. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the algorithm's design, implementation, and evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in various model-related tasks. The resulting improvements in model expressiveness and generalization are significant, offering a promising approach to advancing machine learning.

title: CHATBOTS AND VIRTUAL ASSISTANTS IN PRIVATE HIGHER EDUCATION OF UZBEKISTAN: STUDENT SUPPORT AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY
abstract: Background: The increasing market share of private universities in Uzbekistan necessitates a fundamental improvement in the quality of student support services and organizational workflows.Methods: Utilizing a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, this study investigated thirty-five private higher education institutions across Tashkent, Samarkand, and Fergana. Quantitative metrics tracked chatbot response velocity and first-contact resolution rates, while qualitative interviews with ten IT directors and marketing managers isolated underlying technical limitations.Results: The empirical findings indicate that while automated systems successfully manage seventy-two percent of routine tasks (e.g., tuition contracts and scheduling queries), their effectiveness falls to fourteen percent for complex academic inquiries. A major structural bottleneck is the inadequacy of Natural Language Processing (NLP) models in handling the semantic variations and code-switching characteristic of the contemporary Uzbek language.Conclusion: Private higher education facilities must transition from basic scripted bots to deeply integrated, linguistically sophisticated conversational systems to sustain institutional competitiveness.

title: Distributed Cognitive Maps: Semantic Aggregation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning, termed "Distributed Cognitive Maps" (DCMs). The core idea is to construct a dynamic, self-correcting, and evolving cognitive map through the decentralized sharing and semantic analysis of knowledge across multiple nodes. Unlike traditional, centralized cognitive maps, DCMs leverage the distributed nature of information to overcome limitations regarding scalability, real-time adaptation, and nuanced semantic understanding. The system operates by assigning each node the responsibility of storing and processing localized knowledge. A key mechanism involves using semantic similarity matching and knowledge fusion algorithms to iteratively aggregate these localized pieces of knowledge into a comprehensive global cognitive map. This process is designed to mimic the human cognitive process of integrating disparate pieces of information into a cohesive understanding. The system's ability to learn and adapt through this distributed aggregation is central to its functionality. This paper outlines the architectural design, key algorithms, and potential applications of DCMs, highlighting their advantages over existing approaches.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的动态聚类算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic clustering algorithm based on self-adaptive machine learning. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with data complexity, requiring manual parameter tuning. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the clustering parameters based on feature relationships, allowing the model to effectively capture intricate patterns and improve clustering accuracy and efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of fixed-parameter clustering, offering a more flexible and robust solution for a wide range of datasets. We detail the core mechanism, including the self-adaptive parameter adjustment process and its impact on the resulting clustering results. The algorithm's design leverages the concept of feature importance, ensuring that the clustering focuses on the most relevant dimensions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through rigorous experimental analysis on several benchmark datasets, showcasing its superior performance compared to established methods. Furthermore, we discuss the potential applications of this dynamic clustering technique across various fields.

title: Based on Multi-Scale Geometric Information Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm designed to enhance machine learning precision through the synergistic optimization of multi-scale geometric information. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on single-scale data, limiting their potential for robust and accurate models. Our algorithm introduces a multi-scale geometric information encoding technique, utilizing quantum entanglement and quantum gates to facilitate coordinated optimization of diverse geometric features. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent correlations and patterns within multi-scale datasets to improve model performance across various levels of complexity. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art machine learning models. This work offers a promising path towards more sophisticated and data-driven machine learning solutions.

title: Distributed Learning with Federated Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed learning leveraging Federated Bayesian Networks (FBNs). Traditional federated learning methods struggle with capturing complex, non-independent data distributions, often leading to suboptimal global models. We introduce a framework where multiple devices collaboratively learn a Bayesian Network model through decentralized updates, explicitly addressing these dependency challenges. The core idea is to allow devices to share probabilistic models and inference results, creating a system that adapts to local data characteristics while maintaining data privacy. The framework incorporates techniques for managing network topology, handling heterogeneous data distributions, and ensuring convergence of the collaborative learning process. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline key considerations for practical implementation, highlighting its advantages over conventional federated learning systems. The primary contribution lies in the systematic application of Bayesian Networks to federated learning, providing a robust mechanism for learning from correlated data sources.

title: Dynamic Program Verification with Quantum Algorithm Acceleration
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms to accelerate dynamic program verification (DPV). Dynamic program verification is a computationally intensive process often employed in software verification and formal methods. The core claim presented here is that leveraging quantum algorithms can significantly enhance the efficiency and security of DPV, potentially uncovering vulnerabilities that traditional algorithms might miss. The proposed mechanism involves formulating the DPV problem as a quantum algorithm problem, enabling the utilization of quantum computers for efficient solution. This research explores the theoretical framework and potential impact of such a hybrid approach. Specifically, we examine how quantum superposition and entanglement can be exploited to explore multiple states of the program simultaneously, leading to a faster verification process. The paper details the transformation of DPV state spaces into quantum state spaces and discusses the challenges associated with mapping the computational complexity of DPV onto the capabilities of current and near-term quantum hardware. We conclude by outlining future research directions and the potential for a paradigm shift in software verification.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging probabilistic programming. Traditional causal discovery algorithms frequently rely on restrictive assumptions, leading to limitations in their applicability and robustness, particularly when dealing with complex datasets. This research utilizes probabilistic programming languages to directly model causal relationships and perform inference under a range of assumptions. This framework offers a more principled and flexible methodology, addressing the shortcomings of existing techniques. The core of the approach involves defining causal models using probabilistic programs, specifying prior distributions, and employing inference algorithms to estimate the underlying causal structure. We demonstrate the potential for enhanced robustness and adaptability in causal discovery through this method. The paper outlines the key components of the framework, discusses relevant inference techniques, and presents a conceptual overview of its implementation.

title: Based on Biological Neural Networks Probability Reasoning Engine (BNPR)
abstract: This paper introduces the Biological Neural Networks Probability Reasoning Engine (BNPR), a novel computational engine designed to enhance probability reasoning capabilities, particularly in uncertain and noisy environments. BNPR leverages the principles of biological neural networks, specifically mimicking synaptic plasticity, local connectivity, and information integration mechanisms, to achieve robust and adaptive inference. The core of BNPR lies in its multi-layered neural network architecture, which dynamically adjusts connection weights based on neuron activation probabilities, allowing for continuous learning and knowledge storage. This approach contrasts with traditional probabilistic reasoning engines based on symbolic logic or Bayesian networks, offering a more biologically inspired solution for complex, ambiguous problem-solving. The engine's ability to adapt and learn from data makes it suitable for applications requiring flexible reasoning, such as autonomous systems and intelligent decision-making. We present the design and underlying principles of BNPR, highlighting its potential advantages in handling real-world complexity. ---

title: Automated Proof Strategy Search via Simulated Annealing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to automated program verification by leveraging the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. The core idea is to transform the complex problem of finding an effective proof strategy for a given program into an optimization problem, which is then tackled by SA. Specifically, the system explores the space of possible proof strategies – encompassing techniques like induction, rewriting, and theorem proving – through random perturbations and acceptance of potentially worse solutions. The algorithm aims to iteratively refine the proof strategy until a valid and complete proof is generated. The key contribution lies in the automated search for proof strategies, eliminating the need for manual intervention in the proof process. The system's performance is evaluated through a series of test cases, demonstrating its ability to discover proof strategies that human experts might overlook. The presented method offers a promising direction for enhancing the efficiency and accessibility of program verification.

The core mechanism centers around the iterative adjustment of graph node and edge weights, driven by a feedback loop that continuously improves the system's performance. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to optimize complex systems with minimal human intervention.

title: 基于量子概率模型的超深层神经网络
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum probabilistic models to enhance the efficiency and expressiveness of deep neural networks. Traditional deep learning architectures often struggle with high-dimensional data, necessitating computationally intensive operations. We propose a novel algorithm that integrates quantum probability models into the core computation process of neural networks. This integration leverages the inherent advantages of quantum mechanics, particularly superposition and entanglement, to improve representation learning and parameter estimation. The core mechanism involves mapping the neural network's activation functions and gradient computations into quantum states, allowing for parallel processing and potentially accelerating training and inference. We analyze the theoretical and practical implications of this approach, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations associated with classical neural networks in specific scenarios. The research emphasizes the benefits of quantum-enhanced representations and efficient parameter estimation.

title: Title: Phase Transition Dynamics with Adaptive Resonance Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of phase transitions in materials using a novel system of Adaptive Resonance Networks (ARNs). Phase transition theory provides a framework for understanding how a system undergoes a transformation from one state to another, driven by subtle changes. We propose a system of ARNs designed to simulate and analyze these transitions, dynamically adjusting network parameters to capture the complex evolution of a system. The core mechanism centers around utilizing ARNs to model the evolution of a system based on phase transition principles, enabling accurate predictions of macroscopic behavior from microscopic changes. This work offers a promising approach to quantitatively modeling and understanding phase transition phenomena, leveraging the strengths of ARNs for dynamic simulations.

title: Development and evaluation of an AI-powered conversational agent for small and medium enterprises
abstract: Цель исследования — сделать передовые аналитические инструменты доступными для предприятий малого и среднего бизнеса в сфере электронной коммерции. Для этого были определены аналитические функции, оказывающие наибольшее влияние на эффективность платформ, и разработана доступная система поддержки принятия решений на базе диалогового искусственного интеллекта (ИИ), предназначенная для пользователей без технической подготовки. Исследование проводилось на основе вторичных панельных данных четырех платформ электронной коммерции (Amazon, eBay, Shopify, Flipkart) и семи общедоступных наборов данных. Методы исследования: множественный регрессионный и корреляционный анализ показателей эффективности платформ; методология Design Science Research (исследование через проектирование) для разработки системы; тестирование юзабилити с использованием шкалы System Usability Scale (SUS). Основные результаты: в ходе кросс-платформенного анализа пяти гипотез (H1–H5) выявлена ​​наиболее сильная связь между рекомендациями ИИ и конверсией; разработана диалоговая ИИ-система с двумя режимами работы (на основе правил и с использованием API Claude); оценка системы десятью участниками показала средний балл SUS, равный 71,25, что соответствует целевому показателю приемлемости. Научная новизна заключается в проведении первой оценки на уровне пользователей аналитической системы с диалоговым ИИ, спроектированной и протестированной специально для целевой аудитории — сотрудников малых и средних предприятий электронной коммерции, не обладающих технической квалификацией. Выводы. Задачи диссертационного исследования решены, цель достигнута, а полученные результаты обладают признаками научной новизны.

title: Humans Teaching Machine Learning Agents
abstract: This chapter describes how nonexpert humans can train reinforcement learning (RL) agents. There are numerous ways to learn from human instruction – some have been studied more than others since this is an open field of research. A traditional machine learning approach focuses on the objective performance of the RL agent, optimizing metrics such as training time and reward. Verifying these RL systems is often done with simulated rather than real human input. We believe that to be a limiting approach. In this chapter, we will show: (1) a few methods of humans teaching RL agents; (2) how a great deal of information can be learned from testing these agents with human-subject studies; and (3) how objective performance does not need to be sacrificed in order to create a positive user experience. We can create a much better interactive machine learning system when designing and verifying from a human-centered perspective. We’ll cover different teaching methods, including advice and critique, and how they impact the user experience and objective performance of the agent. We’ll also discus how teaching methods are impacted by many factors, such as rhetorical arguments, immediacy of feedback, and issues of language processing. We’ll also cover a three-step process for the design and verification of interactive machine learning algorithms, and recommendations to improve the human experience.

title: Distilled Continuous Diffusion Language Models Can Write Code in Few Steps---or One
abstract: Language generation is almost universally treated as a sequential process: autoregressive models emit one token at a time, while diffusion language models replace token-level seriality with a long trajectory of iterative refinement. In this work, we introduce PlaidQ, a 0.7B continuous diffusion language model for code generation, and show that its trajectory can be aggressively distilled into only a few denoising steps---or even one, enabling efficient code generation. PlaidQ repurposes a pretrained autoregressive model as a bidirectional denoiser over continuous token embeddings. We distill PlaidQ with distribution matching for few-step generation and paired-trajectory supervision for one-step generation. At matched model scale, PlaidQ is competitive with discrete diffusion language models on code generation. Distillation then shifts the quality--compute frontier: a 16-step student reaches 31.78 and 40.49 pass@10 on HumanEval and MBPP+, surpassing the same PlaidQ teacher sampled for 512 steps. At the extreme, paired-trajectory distillation achieves 7.07 pass@1 on HumanEval with a single denoising step, producing functionally correct programs. Together, these results establish continuous diffusion as a viable path to few-step and one-step code generation. Broadly, continuous diffusion is not merely another representation for language: it provides an interface through which language models can inherit the acceleration and distillation machinery of continuous diffusion modeling. Training and inference code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/pengzhangzhi/plaidq.
